### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/trigger-api`, touching **26** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **7** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-automation/src/flow-credential-channel.ts`, `packages/spec/api-surface/automation.json`, `packages/spec/declaration-map/automation.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**3** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/connectors.mdx`  _(via AutomationServicePluginOptions (symbol, a top-level interface))_
- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via AutomationServicePlugin (symbol, a top-level class), FlowSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/deployment/self-hosting.mdx`  _(via secretRef (literal, a string literal in API_TRIGGER_SECRET_REF_KEY; a string literal in a comment on a changed line))_

⛔ **6** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class), FlowSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-4.mdx`  _(via FlowSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class), AutomationServicePlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-7.mdx`  _(via FlowSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-1.mdx`  _(via FlowSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **7** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-automation/src/flow-credential-channel.ts`, `packages/spec/api-surface/automation.json`, `packages/spec/declaration-map/automation.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **144** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b1790841bb0bf2c7c696e858de51e8105704471a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `426240476fcf853e1d51c33c4b8fe370742dbb8f` — the merge of head `088e442390cafbc51ac080fb3721626e440dfacf` into base `b1790841bb0bf2c7c696e858de51e8105704471a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 426240476fcf853e1d51c33c4b8fe370742dbb8f && git checkout 426240476fcf853e1d51c33c4b8fe370742dbb8f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin b1790841bb0bf2c7c696e858de51e8105704471a 088e442390cafbc51ac080fb3721626e440dfacf && git checkout -B drift-repro b1790841bb0bf2c7c696e858de51e8105704471a && git merge --no-ff 088e442390cafbc51ac080fb3721626e440dfacf

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b1790841bb0bf2c7c696e858de51e8105704471a
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs b1790841bb0bf2c7c696e858de51e8105704471a` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对

ACCEPT · #25675 · `domain:spec` seat 2 (seat post #18549) · `sunhaolin` · session `session_01PC4NPXPgPmpDRG9DdDnyXT` · 2026-10-24T20:10Z · head `088e442390` · report `6388206801` and addendum `6388889634` (on #25675; cloud session `session_01NZJKktPWaz2EZJ95a9XZa8`) · seat review at `TIER_DEFAULT`. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and the path limb hits (`packages/spec/src/automation/**`), so a same-shape `## Contract review` PASS at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` on the landing head is owed. `needs:contract-review` is added in this stroke.

1. **Shape.** Draft, base `main`, first line `Fixes #25675`. The `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: added` and `Ruling-ref: 6386630545` lines are line-initial in the body and in the changeset (`spec`, `lint`, `service-automation`, `trigger-api`, all `minor`). 35 files, +728/−52. No `content/docs/releases/**`.
2. **Governed reading, measured twice.** `check-governed-merges --pr 25703` from this seat's container exits 3: the `skills/**` hit is `references/_index.md`, and the #11705 recompute could not run on an uninstalled tree, so it fails closed. That is a refusal of the prerequisite, not a reading. The reading comes from CI's Governed Surface Queue Guard (job `120964600320`), which installs dependencies: it **LIFTED** `skills/objectstack-automation/references/_index.md` as byte-equal to `gen:skill-refs` recomputed on that tree, so the net diff is **not governed**. That agrees with the dev's local run. `SKILL.md` is back to `origin/main` here. Its four branch commits that touched it show as "unattributed" on the PR-run early warning; the queue judges the landed commit, whose net diff no longer carries the file.
3. **The ruling, measured on the diff.** Letter A of `6386630545`: an `api` start node names its secret, the deployment fills it, `os validate` accepts the reference, and the engine resolves it on every inbound post.
   - `config.secretRef` (`ApiTriggerSecretRefSchema`, a name `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`, not `OS_`, both written as patterns so the JSON Schema carries them). `FlowSchema` refuses three shapes at `nodes[i].config.secretRef`: a reference that is not a name, one beside a literal `secret`, and one on a flow with no `api` trigger.
   - `hookSecretResolver` returns a reader that asks the credential resolver on every call, with no cache. A blank or missing value throws `FlowCredentialUnresolvableError`, which `trigger-api` already answers `503`. An unusable reference, or one beside a literal, yields no reader, so registration refuses rather than arming.
   - "No credential left in the public repository": the showcase literal is gone (`git grep showcase-webhook-secret` finds 0 hits outside CHANGELOGs).
4. **Gates.** `ci-failure --pr 25703` GREEN: 42 check-runs on `088e442390`, all completed, none failed. Local, per the addendum, on this head: 125 derived, 121 exit 0. Four exit 3 (NOT MEASURED, full-build or unshallow prerequisites), and `--ran` shows 0 UNRUN. Package suites (`spec`, `lint`, `trigger-api`, `service-automation`, `metadata-protocol`, `runtime`, plus `test:repo` for `spec`, `runtime` and `rest`) are green at `1abed922` or earlier; the two later commits are an `llms.txt` count and the split. **Ablations**, each restored blob-identical:
   - Disabling the unfilled-name refusal: `api-trigger-secret-ref.test.ts` goes from 5/5 to 2 red (the 503 pin and the env-default pin).
   - Disabling the beside-a-literal refusal: 8/8 to 1 red.
5. **Open questions.**
   - (1) Resolve the name through the `credentialResolver` (env var in the open tier), **A**. The ruling allows 「流程凭据名 / 环境变量名」. The #20790 store is keyed by position, and its only write door is the `/meta` save, which a packaged flow cannot reach (`allowEnvironmentOverlay: false`). So the env-var arm is the one a deployment can fill today. The binding's per-post `resolveSecret` reader is reused as ruled. Whether that reading of 「复用 #20790 已有的写入式流程凭据存储」 holds is the contract review's to judge.
   - (2) Not withheld on read, **A**: the reference is a name, and withholding it would break GET → edit → PUT.
   - (3) Refuse `OS_*`, **A**: a tightening of a key not yet released, with no producer. A hook secret is handed to the signer, so naming `OS_AUTH_SECRET` would hand it out.
   - (4) The skill row, **B**: split into #25708, as ordered in the patch round.
6. **Deviations accepted.** The dev did not edit the PR body after the split, citing the role file. The seat makes that edit in this stroke, as proposed in `6388889634`. Also accepted: `mcp_calls` 3, all reads; relay writes 2 plus 2 this round. The two out-of-scope notes stay in the PR's Acceptance notes / report with no carrier: a pre-#20790 stored literal carried forward beside a new `secretRef` is refused loudly, and an unfilled reference warns only per post.
7. **Landing.** Not governed, 780 changed lines. `hotlong` and `os-zhuang` are still requested reviewers from when the PR touched `SKILL.md`; that request is not a merge gate for this file list. Once a `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` PASS is on record and every check on the then-current head is green, the seat sends `pr_ready` + `automerge_enable` through the relay. #25708 follows after this merges, by the maintainer's hand.
